mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment negatively impacts consumer spending, leading to lower S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If UNRATE exceeds 6.5% but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When employment increases but unemployment also rises, it may signal economic instability, negatively affecting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both PAYEMS and UNRATE move in opposite directions but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 60% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates during tightening cycles can reduce borrowing, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in industrial production suggests strong economic output, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate economic expansion, positively impacting S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST exceeds 1600 but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation combined with low retail sales indicates economic stress, negatively affecting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL is high and RSAFS is low but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 60% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment in late-cycle expansions may not prevent market downturns due to other economic factors.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is below 5% but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 50% of the time.
